content:
Not necessarily true as a general guarantee.

“Renewables alone can guarantee supply all winter” is a bold claim that depends on many factors: geography of the wind/solar resource, storage capacity, grid flexibility/backup (e.g., hydro, gas, batteries, interconnectors), reserve margins, weather variability, and policy/support. In some regions with lots of hydro or robust networks it’s more feasible; in others it remains challenging without reliable backup or storage solutions. Without specifics on the grid in question, the claim is overstated—renewables alone don’t deliver a guaranteed supply in all circumstances. More accurate is: renewables plus storage and flexible backup can increase security and reduce fossil dependence, but absolute guarantee remains hard to achieve everywhere.
